items.summary: On Nov 19, all three major US stock indexes ended sharply lower after Anthropic's record-sized IPO failed to rekindle interest in the AI trade. The S&P 500 lost 2.03% (148.39 points) to close at 7,175.24, marking its fifth straight session of losses and heading toward its steepest weekly drop since April 2025; the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.23% (544.00 points) to 23,885.88, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 2.20% (1,102.71 points) to 49,095.46. Anthropic's debut was priced at US$83 per share on Nov 18 and opened at US$111.50; its valuation briefly topped US$2 trillion before momentum faded as the early spike ebbed. Portfolio manager Jed Ellerbroek of Argent Capital said investors were rebalancing into Anthropic regardless of direction, so he would not read much into the session's movement, though his enthusiasm for AI has cooled on concerns about data centre capex spending and Nvidia. Chipmakers broadly fell after Advanced Micro Devices tumbled following reports that Hunterbrook Capital took a short position; Micron, Broadcom, CoreWeave, Nebius, and Nvidia were all lower, with Nvidia marking its sixth straight session of losses despite an upbeat revenue forecast. Separately, Palo Alto Networks rose on raised 2027 guidance while Walmart dipped after weak sales forecasts. Attention now turns to the Federal Reserve: minutes from the Oct policy meeting showed a desire to curb inflation ahead of rising price indexes, and CME's FedWatch tool prices about a 94% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the December meeting alongside a small but growing odds of a larger move. The Commerce Department is due next week to release its PCE report, with analysts expecting year-on-year core inflation around 3.2%, well above the Fed's 2% target.
items.title: US stocks fell sharply on Nov 19 as Anthropic's IPO failed to revive AI enthusiasm

items.summary: NVIDIA Dynamo is a serving layer positioned between rollout orchestration and inference workers in reinforcement learning (RL) training. It addresses three constraints that slow scaling: uneven workload distribution across GPUs due to differing rollout complexity; repeated context recomputation from shared prompts or repository state; and the need for fresh model weights with acceptable staleness per algorithm requirements. Dynamo's router balances KV cache reuse against worker load, its ModelExpress feature copies weights directly between GPUs over NIXL rather than loading full checkpoints remotely, and delta weight transfer sends a compressed representation of changes so workers reconstruct new weights from an existing base version; the same mechanism lets replacement workers catch up after failures while healthy workers keep generating. The RL framework retains control over generation timing, cached state, readiness checks, interrupted samples, and update coordination. Adoption claims are attributed to specific customers: CoreWeave reports ModelExpress accelerating weight updates by up to 15×, H Company reports reducing average training-step time by up to 20% and GPU-hours by up to 5%, Microsoft AI used Dynamo for post-training rollout inference, Cognition routed rollouts during SWE-1.7 post-training, Prime Intellect uses it for distributed orchestration, and open-source integrations include verl, NeMo RL, Slime, and prime-rl.
items.title: NVIDIA Dynamo serves RL rollouts via routing, ModelExpress weight updates, and failure recovery

items.summary: At Microsoft Ignite, NVIDIA and Microsoft extended their full-stack partnership to cover infrastructure on Azure through Windows PCs. Customers gained access to Azure virtual machines running NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems for reasoning, agentic workloads, training and inference; confidential computing was being extended to bare-metal and rack-scale AI via attestation; and power-efficiency collaboration using MaxLPS aimed at improving data-center performance per available power. Microsoft also cited MLPerf results as evidence of the codesigned infrastructure: in MLPerf Training v6.1 Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on DeepSeek-V3 (the largest scale that round), and in MLPerf Inference v6.1 its GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65. On the model side, Microsoft Foundry expanded serverless Programmed Training and Managed Compute for custom weights; EY reported using Programmed Training to adapt NVIDIA Nemotron open models for classifying corporate purchasing records, improving accuracy on its evaluation dataset by 55% and lowering cost by 15x versus proprietary frontier models. Deployment was broadened beyond the cloud: Foundry Local added reasoning, coding and tool-using agents plus RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs to Azure Local environments; Jetson Thor and Jetson Orin edge platforms were being brought in for industrial use such as machine vision, robotics and autonomous operations; NVIDIA physical AI models including Cosmos were arriving on Foundry Local; and Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark would showcase local large language model experiences. For Cloud PCs (Windows 365), Direct Stream support was planned to deliver up to two 4K streams at 60 frames per second with low latency, though this remained a limited preview open for sign-ups with public preview planned for early 2027. Scientific AI integration added BioNeMo Agent Toolkit and ALCHEMI Toolkit to the Microsoft Discovery catalog, with an initial RFD4-Proteina model from the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design generating candidate protein structures and amino acid sequences. Separately, Microsoft applied NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for reinforcement learning rollout during post-training and RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. All reported accuracy gains, cost reductions, MLPerf rankings and future previews are attributed to their sources or stated as plans rather than established outcomes.
items.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft expand Azure-to-PC AI collaboration at Ignite

items.summary: Anti-AI protesters gathered outside Nasdaq in Times Square, where several were arrested, and at Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters after the company completed what its debut reported as the largest initial public offering in history. The article reports a $2tn valuation and about $81bn raised to develop Claude models, but these figures are attributed to the source rather than independently verified. Around 30 protesters attended the New York rally, carrying signs reading 'STOP TECH OLIGARCHS' and 'FREEZE AI: END ICE, END WAR.' Speakers cited concerns spanning environmental safety, national security, surveillance cameras, and ties between AI research and immigration enforcement. Jes Vesconte framed the protest around profit motives driving multiple crises; Sydney Von Arx of Ban RSI called for a global ban on recursive self-improvement, echoing warnings from Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei that such capabilities could outrun human control. Adam Kaufman referenced WarGames with a sign reading 'The only winning move is not to RACE.' The article presents these as the protesters' claims and concerns rather than established facts about AI risks or the IPO itself.
items.title: Protesters rally against Anthropic's record $2tn IPO in New York and San Francisco

items.summary: House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast released Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) export license information on Thursday, reporting that the Commerce Department approved more than 879,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for sale to China. The committee said requested sales totalled 3.4 million AI chips, with approvals including exports to Chinese military-designated companies such as Alibaba and Tencent; figures run through May 2026 per CNBC. The documents reportedly include requests by Nvidia to use possible chip-smuggling fronts, which Mast called fake companies of concern, though the smuggling characterization is attributed to committee members rather than established fact. Ranking member Gregory Meeks said the panel approved disclosure by unanimous consent and described a contradiction between license-review delays and approvals with little scrutiny; his call for public hearings with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and BIS Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler remains an unfulfilled request, as the Commerce Department did not respond to CNBC's comment request. Separately reported facts include Nvidia stopping shipments of licensed Hopper data center chips (including the H200) after booking $2.4 billion in China sales of that hardware in its fiscal third quarter ending Oct. 25, and Jensen Huang resigning as CEO on Nov. 12 following an admitted affair with a former executive at Megaspeed; these are distinct developments not caused by the disclosure. Lawmakers from both parties have urged new legislation to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI processors to China and other rival nations.
items.title: House Foreign Affairs Committee releases Nvidia and AMD export license data showing large AI chip sales approvals to China
